sub: AI agent for any web page
lead: A browser for iPhone and iPad with one box on every page. Ask the Agent to read, change or automate the page you are on.
c1_p: Type what you want: “make this page dark”, “hide the sidebar”, “summarize this”. The Agent reads the page and changes it with code that runs in the page.
c2_p: Tabs and an address bar, on any site. Pages load in WebKit and you sign in the usual way.
c3_p: The Agent can save a change as a small script for that site. You can read, switch off or delete every script, and import your own user scripts.
c4_p: Summarize the page you are reading, have it read aloud, or talk to the Agent with your voice.
c5_p: Translate a page with Apple’s on-device Translation.
c6_p: Use your own API key with a hosted provider, a model on your local network, or Apple Intelligence on devices that have it.
c7_p: Optional blocking with filter lists that are bundled with the app and compiled on your device.
safe1: The Agent asks before it changes things or sends your login to another site, by default. A Stop button is always on screen while it works.
safe2: Cookie values are not given to the AI unless you turn that on in Settings.
safe3: Text on a web page is treated as untrusted, so a page cannot give the Agent orders.
safe4: Your API keys stay in the iOS Keychain.
note: The Agent works inside the same browser sessions you use. Avoid signing in to banking, payment or main email accounts while you use it.
data_p: There are no WukongMind servers, accounts, analytics or tracking. When you ask the Agent something, the page content it needs goes straight from your device to the AI provider you chose. Read the privacy policy.
hero_alt: The gold Agent ring. Someone asks “Make this page dark”; the ring turns while the Agent works, then closes into a check when the answer is ready.
hero_cap: The gold ring is the Agent. It turns while the Agent works and closes into a check when your answer is ready.
ask_p: The Agent works on the page you have open, on any site.
ask_alt: An iPhone showing a news article. The Agent panel is open: the request “Make this page dark”, two finished steps and the answer “Done. The page is dark now.” The article is now dark.
step1_p: Open the Agent on any site and type it, or say it. There are no menus to learn.
step2_p: The Agent reads the page, then writes JavaScript and CSS and runs them in the page. Each step is listed, and Stop stays on screen.
step3_p: The change happens on the page you are viewing. Like it? Ask the Agent to keep it for your next visit.
demo_answer: Done. The page is dark now.
addr_p: Tap the address field and Home appears over the page. Type an address, a search or a request. The first row is what Return does.
addr_l2: A question or an instruction goes to the Agent.
addr_l3: Anything else is a web search.
addr_alt: An iPhone with the address field in use. Home covers the page, “hide the sidebar” is typed, and the first suggestion reads “Ask the Agent: hide the sidebar”, above a web search for the same words.
script_p: The Agent can keep a change as a small script for that site, and you can import standard user scripts from a link. Before anything is added you see where it comes from, the sites it runs on, what it can use and the full code.
script_alt: An iPhone showing the Add script sheet for a script named Tidy Pages: its source, the site it runs on, what it can use, its code, and the buttons “Add and turn on” and “Add, keep off”.
end_p: Open any site and say what you want.
